data.one_liner: A lightweight Dart framework for building server‑side web apps, APIs, databases and WebSockets.
data.what_it_does: Finch provides routing, database integration (MongoDB, MySQL, SQLite), WebSocket support, cron jobs, and static file serving for server‑side Dart applications. It also includes features like i18n, form validation, and OpenAPI documentation generation.
use_when: You need a full‑stack server framework in pure Dart
You want built‑in support for multiple databases and WebSockets
You prefer a single package that handles routing, config, and utilities
avoid_when: You are building only a client‑side Flutter app
You need a highly modular micro‑library rather than an all‑in‑one framework
You require deep integration with Firebase or other hosted backends
strengths: Unified API for routing, DB, and WebSockets
Supports MongoDB, MySQL, SQLite out of the box
Built‑in i18n, cron jobs, and OpenAPI generation
Fast performance with native Dart compilation
weaknesses: Primarily server‑side; not suited for mobile UI code
Learning curve if unfamiliar with server concepts
data.setup_notes: Add finch to pubspec, run `dart pub get`; no special permissions needed. Use FinchApp to configure routes, DB connections, and start the server.
